key_insight: Flexible Hawkes processes largely close the reported gap with neural temporal point processes, whose gains mainly concern when events occur rather than which events occur.
clinical_relevance: For modeling disease histories and ICU event sequences, intensity flexibility may matter as much as model class, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Compared increasingly flexible Poisson and Hawkes processes with neural models for autoregressive next-event prediction.
Evaluated a Transformer with a spline-based intensity head.
Separated log-likelihood into event-time and event-type terms.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered five established benchmarks and two large-scale medical tasks from UK Biobank and MIMIC-IV; only MIMIC-IV showed a retained neural advantage in the event-type term.
watch_item: Next-event prediction results do not establish prospective clinical benefit or readiness for deployment.
paper_title: Flexible Intensities Matter: A Comprehensive Re-evaluation of Hawkes Processes and Neural Temporal Point Processes
